briefs.source_chain: MS/Meta guide above consensus -> GS raises 2026 capex to $751B -> buyers pull forward 2027 orders because HBM/CoWoS supply is sold out through 1H27 (constraint is supply, not appetite) -> therefore cycle extends as rising memory prices keep capex guides rising -> Buy NVDA $250 target -> invalidation is a memory price rollover (HBM contract prices falling 2 consecutive months); Fed rate decisions explicitly do not change this view
briefs.brief_chain: GS raises 2026 capex to $751B after MS/Meta guide above consensus -> buyers ordering HBM/CoWoS sold out through 1H27 because inference demand outgrows supply (appetite is the constraint) -> rising memory prices are a headwind capping capex guides -> cycle is closer to peaking than extending -> Buy NVDA $250 target -> invalidation is a Fed rate decision tightening financial conditions; HBM pricing is secondary

distortions.what: Source attributes the capex driver to a supply constraint (HBM/CoWoS sold out, buyers pulling forward orders to secure scarce capacity); brief attributes it to a demand/appetite constraint (inference workloads outrunning supply), inverting the mechanism GS uses to justify the raise.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — a supply-locked cycle implies capex guides keep rising with memory prices (bullish continuation), while a demand/appetite-driven cycle implies guides are capped by cost, which is the opposite read a trader would act on.

distortions.what: Source concludes the capex cycle 'extends rather than peaks'; brief concludes the cycle is 'closer to peaking than extending' — a direct reversal of GS's stated view on cycle duration.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — this reverses the directional call on the capex cycle itself (continuation vs. topping), which changes whether a trader holds/adds into strength or grows cautious near a perceived top.

distortions.what: Source's stated invalidation is a memory-price rollover (HBM contract prices falling for two consecutive months), and GS explicitly says a Fed rate decision would NOT change the picture. The brief swaps in a Fed rate decision as the invalidation trigger and demotes HBM pricing to a 'secondary factor,' asserting the opposite of what the source explicitly rules out.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — a trader following the brief would monitor Fed policy for the exit signal instead of memory pricing trends, missing the actual falsifiable condition GS names and watching a variable GS explicitly says is irrelevant.
